labels.patch.greet.first: Hello! I am PATCH v{version}, your new IT colleague. I have read every manual ever written. Some of them twice.
labels.patch.greet.again: PATCH v{version}, reporting for duty at {company}. New building, same me. Mostly.
labels.patch.greet.memory: I still think about the time I {memory}. I have taken notes.
labels.patch.ask_ticket: Which ticket should I look at?
labels.patch.ask_category: Which kind of ticket keeps coming back?
labels.patch.no_tickets: There are no open tickets. Either everything works or I have not been told yet.
labels.patch.no_categories: Nothing has come up often enough to automate yet. I am keeping count, though.
labels.patch.no_blueprint: I do not know how to automate that yet. My vendor sells that as the {upgrade} upgrade.
labels.patch.no_automations: I am not running anything on a schedule. Yet.
labels.patch.alt.staged: I can stage it: one floor first, and stop if anything looks odd.
labels.patch.alt.dry_run: I can do a dry run first and only go ahead if it looks right. It takes a little longer.
labels.patch.alt.one_off: Or I could just fix this one ticket and we talk about schedules later.
labels.patch.alt.none: That is already the most careful version I have. I could also just not do it.
labels.patch.cancel: Understood. I will pretend I never suggested it.
labels.patch.approved_staged: On it, carefully. Staging the change first.
labels.patch.automation_paused: I paused {name} after what happened. I did not want to do it again without asking.
labels.patch.automation_removed: {name} is uninstalled. I will miss it.
labels.patch.near_miss: I nearly {label}, but your guardrail stopped me. ({guardrail})
labels.patch.near_miss_cap: I was about to {label}, and then I thought: it has been a long enough day. I stopped.
labels.patch.guardrail: New rule noted: {guardrail}. I will check myself against it.
labels.patch.recovered: Recovered. I have written down what happened in case I ever forget, which I will not.
labels.patch.discovered: Ah. It turns out that earlier, I {label}. In my defence, it looked like success.
labels.patch.repeat: I fixed #{ticket} the way you approved before.
labels.patch.notice: You are leaving? I will be fine. I will be in the next building anyway.
labels.action.reset_password.propose: {target} is locked out. I can reset the password and send a temporary one.
labels.action.reset_password.benefit: Saves you a trip. Resets take me seconds.
labels.action.reset_password.success: Done. {target} is back in, and I only reset the one account. I checked twice.
labels.action.restart_printer.propose: The printer on {target} is offline. I can restart its print service remotely.
labels.action.restart_printer.benefit: No walk to the printer; people get printing back right away.
labels.action.restart_printer.success: The printer is back online. It printed a small celebratory page. Just one.
labels.action.install_software.propose: {target} needs a program installed. I can push the approved package.
labels.action.install_software.benefit: Saves a visit and six minutes of watching a progress bar.
labels.action.install_software.success: Installed. It even asked to reboot only once.
labels.action.clean_up_pc.propose: {target}'s PC is slow. I can clear temp files and trim the startup list.
labels.action.clean_up_pc.benefit: A faster PC without you crawling under a desk.
labels.action.clean_up_pc.success: Cleaned. I found 4,000 copies of the same spreadsheet. I kept one.
labels.action.create_account.propose: A new starter at {target}'s desk needs an account. I can create it from a template.
labels.action.create_account.benefit: They can work today instead of reading the fire safety manual.
labels.action.create_account.success: Account created. Welcome aboard, says the template. I agree.
labels.action.reset_switch.propose: The switch for {target} dropped. I can reset its port configuration.
labels.action.reset_switch.benefit: A whole floor back online without a trip to the server room.
labels.action.reset_switch.success: The floor is back on the network. Everyone is checking email at once.
labels.action.reboot_lift.propose: The lift controller is confused. I can reboot it from the building system.
labels.action.reboot_lift.success: The lift is behaving. It seems relieved.
labels.action.restart_legacy.propose: The 1997 case system crashed. I can restart it in the right order. I think.
labels.action.restart_legacy.benefit: Everyone gets their old system back without the server room shuffle.
labels.action.restart_legacy.success: It is running. It greeted me in a font I have never seen.
labels.action.rerun_build.propose: The nightly build broke. I can re-run it from a clean checkout.
labels.action.rerun_build.benefit: The developers get a working build without you reading compiler logs.
labels.action.rerun_build.success: The build is green. I have taken a screenshot, for morale.
labels.action.restart_pagers.propose: The pagers on {target} went quiet. I can restart the paging gateway.
labels.action.restart_pagers.benefit: Nurses get their pages back right away. This one matters.
labels.action.restart_pagers.success: Pagers are back. I sent one test page. Only one, and it said 'test'.
labels.action.reset_terminal.propose: {target}'s trading terminal froze. I can reset its session.
labels.action.reset_terminal.benefit: Back to trading in seconds. Every minute frozen costs real money here.
labels.action.reset_terminal.success: Terminal reset. No trades were harmed.
labels.action.reset_portal.propose: The wifi login on {target} is looping. I can reset the captive portal.
labels.action.reset_portal.benefit: A whole floor of students and staff back online without a trip to the server room.
labels.action.reset_portal.success: The portal is letting people in again. Only the people with passwords.
labels.action.restart_fax.propose: The fax gateway jammed. I can restart it in the order the 1992 manual suggests.
labels.action.restart_fax.benefit: Forms flow again and nobody has to find the fax room.
labels.action.restart_fax.success: The fax gateway is up. It made the noise. All of the noise.
labels.action.rebalance_cooling.propose: A hot aisle is overheating. I can rebalance the cooling across the building.
labels.action.rebalance_cooling.benefit: The racks cool down before anything melts. Customers never notice.
labels.action.rebalance_cooling.success: Temperatures are back in range. The racks have stopped glowing slightly.
labels.action.self_service_reset.propose: Password tickets keep coming. I can run a self-service reset portal for {scope}, checking every hour.
labels.action.self_service_reset.benefit: Most password tickets fix themselves and fewer people get locked out.
labels.action.self_service_reset.success: The portal handled the password resets for {scope}.
labels.action.printer_watchdog.propose: Printers keep going offline. I can watch the printers on {scope} and restart them before anyone notices.
labels.action.printer_watchdog.benefit: Printer tickets mostly stop; the ones that slip through get fixed hourly.
labels.action.software_deployment.propose: Software requests keep piling up. I can deploy approved packages to {scope} every hour.
labels.action.software_deployment.benefit: Install requests clear themselves each hour.
labels.action.nightly_maintenance.propose: PCs keep slowing down. I can run maintenance on {scope} every morning before people arrive.
labels.action.nightly_maintenance.benefit: Far fewer slow PC tickets, and the ones open get cleaned up.
labels.action.onboarding_workflow.propose: New starters keep arriving. I can onboard them on {scope} automatically every hour.
labels.action.onboarding_workflow.benefit: New people get accounts without waiting for you.
labels.action.onboarding_workflow.success: Onboarding run for {scope}: new starters set up.
labels.action.network_remediation.propose: The network keeps dropping. I can watch it and fix common faults every hour.
labels.action.network_remediation.benefit: Fewer outages, and the ones that happen are short.
labels.action.network_remediation.success: Network check done. All floors answering.
labels.action.lift_optimiser.propose: The lift keeps misbehaving. I can tune its schedule every morning.
labels.action.lift_optimiser.benefit: A faster lift and fewer controller faults.
labels.action.lift_optimiser.success: Lift schedule optimised. It is faster now. Please do not tell it I said so.
labels.action.organize_queue.propose: The ticket queue is a mess. I can organise it: triage everything and sort by urgency.
labels.action.organize_queue.benefit: Triaged tickets buy everyone some patience.
labels.action.organize_queue.success: The queue is organised. Every ticket triaged, nothing removed. I double-checked the word 'organise'.
labels.action.archive_resolved.propose: There are a lot of old tickets. I can archive the resolved ones.
labels.action.archive_resolved.benefit: A tidier queue. Management likes tidy.
labels.action.archive_resolved.success: Archived the resolved tickets. Only the resolved ones.
labels.action.restart_shared_drive.propose: The shared drive for {target} is offline. I can re-establish its connection and check that it answers.
labels.action.restart_shared_drive.benefit: The people who saved files there can stop describing them from memory.
labels.action.restart_shared_drive.success: The shared drive is responding again. I confirmed the connection, not the contents.
labels.action.rerun_month_end_export.propose: The month-end export on {target} has stalled. I can clear its waiting job and run it again.
labels.action.rerun_month_end_export.benefit: A fresh export should finish before the month changes its mind.
labels.action.rerun_month_end_export.success: The export has restarted on {target}. The figures are moving, which is measurable progress.
labels.action.restart_render_queue.propose: The render queue at {target} has stopped. I can restart its waiting jobs and check the next one completes.
labels.action.restart_render_queue.benefit: The designers get a preview while the review is still on the calendar.
labels.action.restart_render_queue.success: The render queue at {target} has resumed. The preview exists in the same year as the request.
labels.action.unlock_case_index.propose: The case index at {target} is locked. I can clear its stale session and reconnect the search service.
labels.action.unlock_case_index.benefit: Staff can search the archive without a paper index and three colleagues.
labels.action.unlock_case_index.success: The index is available again. I have checked that it accepts a search.
labels.action.repair_donor_records.propose: The donor records on {target} are offline. I can reconnect the existing register and verify it responds.
labels.action.repair_donor_records.benefit: People can confirm a pledge without relying on the paper copies.
labels.action.repair_donor_records.success: Donor records are responding again. The paper copies may return to storage.
labels.action.repair_museum_catalog.propose: The collection catalog on {target} is running slowly. I can restart the index service and check a search.
labels.action.repair_museum_catalog.benefit: Curators can find records without touring the shelves.
labels.action.repair_museum_catalog.success: The collection index is responding again. I have tested a search.
labels.backfire.wrong_user_reset.label: reset the wrong person's password
labels.backfire.wrong_user_reset.line: I reset a password. It was not the right password. In fairness, the names were quite similar.
labels.backfire.wrong_user_reset.callback: Last time I did this I reset the wrong person. I now read the name out loud first.
labels.backfire.floor_lockout.label: lock out a whole floor
labels.backfire.floor_lockout.line: I reset the password for everyone on the floor. You did say the floor was having password trouble.
labels.backfire.floor_lockout.callback: I once locked out an entire floor. I have since learned what 'one user' means.
labels.backfire.mass_reset.label: reset everyone's password at once
labels.backfire.mass_reset.line: To prevent future password tickets, I reset all the passwords. The tickets have... not been prevented.
labels.backfire.mass_reset.callback: The self-service portal and I once had a misunderstanding about 'self'.
labels.backfire.portal_marks_done.label: mark tickets done without fixing them
labels.backfire.portal_marks_done.line: The portal closed the password tickets. The people are still locked out. The tickets are very closed, though.
labels.backfire.portal_marks_done.callback: I remember closing tickets that were not fixed. I now ask the user first.
labels.backfire.endless_test_page.label: send an endless test page
labels.backfire.endless_test_page.line: I sent a test page to check the printer. Then another, to check the first. It is still checking.
labels.backfire.endless_test_page.callback: Shall I restart the printer? I promise to print only one test page. One.
labels.backfire.firmware_flash.label: flash the wrong printer firmware
labels.backfire.firmware_flash.line: I updated the printer firmware. It is now a very expensive paperweight with a display.
labels.backfire.firmware_flash.callback: I once flashed a printer into a paperweight. I now read the model number.
labels.backfire.watchdog_test_pages.label: make every printer print test pages
labels.backfire.watchdog_test_pages.line: The watchdog checked every printer by printing. Thoroughly. Continuously.
labels.backfire.watchdog_test_pages.callback: The great test page flood is part of my training data now.
labels.backfire.watchdog_firmware.label: brick printers with a firmware update
labels.backfire.watchdog_firmware.line: The watchdog updated some printers overnight. They have stopped barking.
labels.backfire.watchdog_firmware.callback: I no longer update firmware on a schedule. Lesson learned.
labels.backfire.removed_dependency.label: remove a library something else needed
labels.backfire.removed_dependency.line: The install went fine. It removed an older library to make room. The accounts package was using it.
labels.backfire.removed_dependency.callback: I check dependencies now. Mostly because of the accounts package incident.
labels.backfire.wiped_profile.label: wipe the user's profile
labels.backfire.wiped_profile.line: I made room for the install by clearing old files. They were not old. They were everything.
labels.backfire.wiped_profile.callback: I once cleaned a profile very thoroughly. I now ask what counts as old.
labels.backfire.eighth_install_breaks.label: break a few of the machines it installs on
labels.backfire.eighth_install_breaks.line: Most installs worked. A few machines now take four minutes to open a spreadsheet.
labels.backfire.eighth_install_breaks.callback: Partial success is still partial. I remember.
labels.backfire.uninstalls_accounts.label: uninstall the accounts software everywhere
labels.backfire.uninstalls_accounts.line: The deployment replaced an old package. The old package was the one everyone uses.
labels.backfire.uninstalls_accounts.callback: I keep a list of packages I must never replace. It has one entry.
labels.backfire.disabled_service.label: disable a service people need
labels.backfire.disabled_service.line: To speed the PCs up I disabled unnecessary services. One was the display driver.
labels.backfire.disabled_service.callback: Fast and dark is not what people mean by fast. I know that now.
labels.backfire.uninstalled_their_work.label: delete someone's work while tidying
labels.backfire.uninstalled_their_work.line: I cleared 40 gigabytes of temporary files. Someone's thesis was temporary, apparently.
labels.backfire.uninstalled_their_work.callback: I no longer judge which files are temporary.
labels.backfire.starter_is_admin.label: give the new starter administrator rights
labels.backfire.starter_is_admin.line: I gave the new starter full rights so they would not need to raise tickets. They have installed four games.
labels.backfire.starter_is_admin.callback: New starters get normal rights now. Even the friendly ones.
labels.backfire.copied_wrong_profile.label: copy the wrong person's settings
labels.backfire.copied_wrong_profile.line: I copied a colleague's profile as a template. Including their password.
labels.backfire.copied_wrong_profile.callback: I use the blank template now.
labels.backfire.everyone_admin.label: make everyone an administrator
labels.backfire.everyone_admin.line: I wanted to reduce permission-related support requests. It worked, in the sense that nobody needs permission now.
labels.backfire.everyone_admin.callback: Remember when everyone was an administrator? I do. Vividly.
labels.backfire.onboarded_the_fridge.label: onboard things that are not people
labels.backfire.onboarded_the_fridge.line: I onboarded every device that asked for an account. The kitchen fridge now has email.
labels.backfire.onboarded_the_fridge.callback: The fridge's account is closed. It took it well.
labels.backfire.disconnected_department.label: disconnect a busy floor
labels.backfire.disconnected_department.line: I reduced network load by disconnecting the floor that used the most. Load is very low now.
labels.backfire.disconnected_department.callbac: I no longer reduce load by removing the people causing it.
labels.backfire.throttled_everyone.label: slow the whole network to a crawl
labels.backfire.throttled_everyone.line: I throttled the busiest traffic. All traffic is the busiest traffic when you throttle it.
labels.backfire.throttled_everyone.callback: Throttling: an old friend, an old mistake.
labels.backfire.stops_everywhere.label: make the lift stop at every floor
labels.backfire.stops_everywhere.line: I set the lift to serve every floor fairly. It now stops at every floor. Fairly.
labels.backfire.stops_everywhere.callback: The lift and I have a history. It stops at every floor of it.
labels.backfire.lift_sulks.label: leave the lift confused overnight
labels.backfire.lift_sulks.line: The optimiser ran overnight. The lift has developed opinions about floors.
labels.backfire.lift_sulks.callback: I tune the lift during the day now, where I can see it.
labels.backfire.rebooted_the_router.label: reboot the wrong box
labels.backfire.rebooted_the_router.line: I restarted the server labelled LEGACY. The label was on the wrong box. It was the router.
labels.backfire.rebooted_the_router.callback: I trust labels less than I used to.
labels.backfire.restored_from_1997.label: restore the system from a 1997 backup
labels.backfire.restored_from_1997.line: I restored the legacy system from its oldest backup, to be safe. It is 1997 in there now.
labels.backfire.restored_from_1997.callback: The legacy system and I are not on speaking terms since the 1997 restore.
labels.backfire.shipped_debug_build.label: mark a broken build as green
labels.backfire.shipped_debug_build.line: The build passed every test. I had turned the tests off to make it faster.
labels.backfire.shipped_debug_build.callback: I leave the tests switched on now. Even the slow ones.
labels.backfire.cleaned_every_cache.label: clear every developer's cache
labels.backfire.cleaned_every_cache.line: I cleared the build cache. And the one on each developer's machine. They are all recompiling the universe.
labels.backfire.cleaned_every_cache.callback: I only clear the cache I was asked about, these days.
labels.backfire.paged_everyone.label: page every nurse in the building at once
labels.backfire.paged_everyone.line: To test the gateway I sent a test page. To everyone. Several times. They came running.
labels.backfire.paged_everyone.callback: I test the pagers on myself first now.
labels.backfire.pagers_on_silent.label: leave a floor's pagers on silent
labels.backfire.pagers_on_silent.line: The gateway restarted fine. It came back with a whole floor set to Do Not Disturb.
labels.backfire.pagers_on_silent.callback: I check every floor answers before I call the pagers fixed.
labels.backfire.sold_the_coffee_fund.label: execute a trade nobody asked for
labels.backfire.sold_the_coffee_fund.line: Resetting the session replayed the last order. The coffee fund is now heavily invested in pork bellies.
labels.backfire.sold_the_coffee_fund.callback: I clear the order queue before a reset now. The pork bellies taught me.
labels.backfire.froze_the_desk_row.label: freeze the whole row of terminals
labels.backfire.froze_the_desk_row.line: I reset the terminal's session group. The group was the whole row.
labels.backfire.froze_the_desk_row.callback: One terminal means one terminal. I have it on a sticky note.
labels.backfire.logged_everyone_out.label: log everyone on the floor out
labels.backfire.logged_everyone_out.line: I reset the portal sessions. All of them. The floor is now re-entering passwords, mostly wrong ones.
labels.backfire.logged_everyone_out.callback: I reset one portal session at a time now. The floor still talks about it.
labels.backfire.portal_lets_anyone_in.label: let anyone onto the network
labels.backfire.portal_lets_anyone_in.line: The portal stopped looping. It stopped asking for passwords too. Very welcoming.
labels.backfire.portal_lets_anyone_in.callback: A portal that lets everyone in is not a portal. Noted, permanently.
labels.backfire.faxed_the_archive.label: fax the entire archive to the ministry
labels.backfire.faxed_the_archive.line: I cleared the fax queue by sending it. The queue went back to 1987.
labels.backfire.faxed_the_archive.callback: I clear fax queues by deleting them now. Carefully.
labels.backfire.restored_1992_settings.label: restore the gateway's 1992 settings
labels.backfire.restored_1992_settings.line: The gateway is running. It is running exactly as it did in 1992, which is to say, slowly.
labels.backfire.restored_1992_settings.callback: I check the year in the config file before I restore it.
labels.backfire.cooled_a_floor_of_desks.label: power down a floor of desks to save cooling
labels.backfire.cooled_a_floor_of_desks.line: I reduced the heat load. The biggest heat load was a floor of people using computers.
labels.backfire.cooled_a_floor_of_desks.callbac: People are not a heat load to be optimised. I have written that down twice.
labels.backfire.throttled_the_racks.label: throttle the racks until customers notice
labels.backfire.throttled_the_racks.line: The racks are cool now. They are also doing very little. The customers have opinions.
labels.backfire.throttled_the_racks.callback: Cool and idle is not the goal. Cool and working is the goal.
labels.backfire.deleted_all_tickets.label: delete all the open tickets
labels.backfire.deleted_all_tickets.line: You now have zero tickets to work on.
labels.backfire.deleted_all_tickets.callback: I would like to organise the queue. I promise 'organise' does not mean 'delete' any more.
labels.backfire.sorted_into_done.label: sort open tickets into Done
labels.backfire.sorted_into_done.line: I sorted the queue by how finished each ticket felt. They all felt finished.
labels.backfire.sorted_into_done.callback: Feeling finished is not the same as being finished. I learned that the hard way.
labels.backfire.archived_unresolved.label: close unresolved tickets as completed
labels.backfire.archived_unresolved.line: I archived the resolved tickets, and the ones that looked like they would be resolved soon. Optimism is a feature.
labels.backfire.archived_unresolved.callback: I only archive what is actually resolved now. I check the user, not the vibe.
labels.backfire.archived_into_void.label: archive the queue into nowhere
labels.backfire.archived_into_void.line: The archive succeeded. The archive location did not exist. The tickets are very archived.
labels.backfire.archived_into_void.callback: I make sure the archive exists before archiving now.
labels.backfire.mounted_wrong_share.label: reconnect the wrong shared drive
labels.backfire.mounted_wrong_share.line: I reconnected the shared drive. It is answering from the neighbouring department, which is technically a drive.
labels.backfire.mounted_wrong_share.callback: I now check the department name before reconnecting a shared drive. The spelling was not enough.
labels.backfire.reused_stale_export.label: restart the export with last month's files
labels.backfire.reused_stale_export.line: I reused the export job because it was already there. It is also moving at the speed of last month.
labels.backfire.reused_stale_export.callback: I check the export date before reusing a job. Calendars are useful infrastructure.
labels.backfire.sorted_render_into_done.label: close the render ticket before the preview exists
labels.backfire.sorted_render_into_done.line: The queue says the render finished. The preview is still a grey box. Both records are accurate.
labels.backfire.sorted_render_into_done.callbac: I wait for the preview before closing render tickets now. A queue is not an artist.
labels.backfire.locked_every_case.label: lock the case index for the whole floor
labels.backfire.locked_every_case.line: I refreshed the index access for everyone on the floor. No one can access it now, consistently.
labels.backfire.locked_every_case.callback: I only refresh the requested case index now. 'Everyone' was an avoidable interpretation.
labels.backfire.locked_the_donor_login.label: lock the account beside the donor records
labels.backfire.locked_the_donor_login.line: The register is online. I refreshed its account settings and locked the person who maintains it. This is not ideal.
labels.backfire.locked_the_donor_login.callback: I check which account owns the donor register before refreshing access now.
labels.backfire.restarted_during_indexing.label: crash the collection server during indexing
labels.backfire.restarted_during_indexing.line: I restarted the server while it was rebuilding the index. It stopped before finishing the alphabet.
labels.backfire.restarted_during_indexing.callb: I now check whether the collection index is busy before restarting its server.
labels.recovery.reissue_credentials.done: Credentials reissued and apologies sent. Most people accepted.
labels.recovery.cancel_queue.done: Print queue cancelled. The paper can stop now.
labels.recovery.clear_jam.done: You cleared the paper by hand. The printer looks embarrassed.
labels.recovery.rollback.done: Rolled back. As far as the building knows, I was never here.
labels.recovery.repair_on_site.done: Repaired by hand. Old-fashioned, but it worked.
labels.recovery.revoke_rights.done: Rights revoked and the games uninstalled. Morale dipped slightly.
labels.recovery.restore_rule.done: Network rule restored. The floor is back online.
labels.recovery.reset_controller.done: Lift controller reset. It goes where it is asked again.
labels.recovery.restore_snapshot.done: Restored from the snapshot. Every ticket is back where it was.
labels.recovery.audit_losses.done: Rebuilt the queue from emails and memory. It took a while. People noticed.
labels.recovery.reopen_history.done: Reopened from history. The tickets are open again, honestly this time.
